Appeal No. 12-R/10 of 07/05, dated 13.01.2009, vide which, learned appellate court has upheld the judgment of conviction passed by the Court of learned Sub Divisional Judicial Magistrate, Rohru in Cr. Case No. 71-3 of 2004 dated 7.12.2004, whereby the petitioner was convicted by the learned trial Court for commission of offence punishable under Section 16(1)(a)(ii) read with Section 7(iii) of Prevention of Food Adulteration Act (hereinafter referred to as 'P.F.A. sentences.text: The case of the prosecution was that on 21.4.2004 .
Food Inspector L.D. Thakur inspected the premises i.e. Sharma Sweets Shop, Rohru at about 2:00 p.m. and found the present petitioner conducting business of said sweet shop.
The items which were kept for sale to the general public included "Laddu, Jalebi, Burfi and Samosas etc."

etc. Food Inspector asked the of petitioner to produce P.F.A. licence issued in his favour for sale of food articles, as was required under Rule 50 of P.F.A. Rules, rt 1955, however, accused failed to produce any licence issued in his favour to conduct the abovementioned business for the years 2004-2005.
Besides this, the sweets were kept uncovered exposed to rain, dust and flies.
Accordingly, Food Inspector prepared a spot map which was duly signed by the accused and Food Inspector himself.

Thereafter, Food Inspector placed documents of the accused before Chief Medical Officer, Shimla who was empowered to give written consent under Section 20 of the P.F.A. Act to launch prosecution against the accused.
In this background, Food Inspector filed complaint against the accused under Section 16(1)(a)(ii) of P.F.A. Act.

3. As a prima facie case was made out against the accused for commission of offence punishable under Section 16(1)(a)(II) read with Section 7(iii) of P.F.A. Act, 1954, accordingly notice of accusation was put to him to which accused pleaded not guilty and claimed trial.

4. On the basis of material produced on record by the .
prosecution, learned trial court held that the prosecution was able to prove its case against the accused beyond all reasonable doubt for commission of offence punishable under Sections 16(1)(a)(II) read with Section 7(iii) of P.F.A. Act, 1954 and sentenced him to undergo simple imprisonment for three months of and to pay fine of ` 500/-.
5. Feeling aggrieved by the said judgment passed by rt learned trial court, accused preferred an appeal before learned appellate court.

Learned appellate court upheld the judgment of conviction and sentence imposed upon the present petitioner by the learned trial court and dismissed the appeal.
6.
Feeling aggrieved by the said two judgments passed by learned courts below, the accused has preferred the present revision petition.
7. I have heard learned counsel for the parties and have also gone through the records of the case as well as the judgments passed by both the learned courts below.

8. It stands established on the basis of material produced on record by the prosecution that on 21.4.2004, when Food Inspector L.D. Thakur inspected the Sharma Sweets Shop at Rohru wherein the present petitioner was conducting the business of sweet shop, he was not possessing any licence for sale of food articles which were being sold in the shop as is the requirement under Rule 50 of Ram Krishan vs State Of Himachal Pradesh on 26 October, 2016 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/41634672/
2 P.F.A. Rules, 1955.

sentences.text:
It is duly borne out from the records that the complainant was duly appointed as .
Food Inspector on the relevant date and was competent to inspect the premises of the accused as well as to launch prosecution in case sanction was duly accorded by the competent authority.

It further stands proved on record by the prosecution that Chief Medical Officer, Shimla was competent to of accord written consent for the purposes of launching prosecution as is contemplated under Section 20 of the P.F.A. Act and
it was rt on the basis of the written consent accorded in this regard by Chief Medical Officer, Shimla that the prosecution was launched against the accused by the complainant.

It is apparent and evident from the findings returned by learned trial court as well as by learned appellate court that the petitioner in fact was conducting his business of sweet shop in violation of the provisions of P.F.A. Act, as he was not having any valid licence as on 21.4.2004.
The findings returned in this regard by both learned courts below could not be proved to be either perverse or contrary to the records by the learned counsel for the petitioner.
The factum of the prosecution not possessing a valid licence as on 21.4.2004 to conduct the business of sweet shop could not be refuted by the learned counsel for the petitioner.

His contention that the learned trial court had brushed aside non compliance of Section 10(7) of the P.F.A. Act and that non association of an independent witness had vitiated the entire proceedings and had resulted in miscarriage of justice is without any merit.

This is for the reason that the factum of the petitioner .
conducting the business of sweet shop without any valid licence is an established fact and even otherwise to demonstrate this fact the provisions of Sub Section 7 of Section 10 of P.F.A. Act, 1954 have no relevance.

It is not a case where any sample was taken because in the present case the allegation against the of petitioner was that he was running the business without a valid licence and this fact stands duly proved by the prosecution rt because the onus to have proved that he was having a valid licence to conduct the business of sweet shop could have been easily discharged by the petitioner by producing a licence issued in his favour by the competent authority before the Food Inspector which he did not produce, as he was not having any valid licence as on 21.4.2004 to conduct the said business.

9. A perusal of the judgments passed by both learned courts below demonstrate that all these aspects have been taken into consideration by both learned courts below and it cannot be said that the conclusions which have been arrived at by both learned courts below on the basis of material produced on record by the prosecution were either perverse or were not borne out from the material on record.

Even during the course of arguments, learned counsel for the petitioner could not point out as to what was the perversity with the findings returned by both learned courts below or which particular finding returned either by learned trial court or by learned appellate court was not borne out from the records of the case.

.

sentences.text: It is well settled law that the jurisdiction of High Court in revision is severely restricted and it cannot embark upon re- appreciation of evidence.

The High Court in revision cannot in absence of error on a point of law,
re-appreciate evidence and reverse a finding of law.
of 11.

It has been further held by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Janta Dal Vs. H.S. Chowdhury &
others, 1992 (4) SCC rt 305 that the object of the revisional jurisdiction was to confer power upon superior criminal Courts a kind of paternal or supervisory jurisdiction in order to correct miscarriage of justice arising from misconception of law, irregularity of procedure, neglect of proper precaution or apparent harshness of treatment which has resulted on the one hand, or on the other hand in some undeserved hardship to individuals.

entities.text:
Janta Dal Vs. H.S. Chowdhury &
others, 1992 (4) SCC rt 305
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 12. Thus it can be safely inferred that this Court has to exercise its revisional powers sparingly.
Though, this Court is not required to act as a Court of appeal, however, at the same time it is the duty of the Court to correct manifest illegality resulting in gross miscarriage of justice.
However, I do not find any manifest illegality with the judgments passed by the learned Courts below in the present case.
13. In view of the above discussion, I am of the considered view that there is neither any perversity nor any infirmity with the judgments passed by the learned Courts below.

. 
In this view of the matter, the present revision petition is dismissed being devoid of any merit.
Pending miscellaneous application(s), if any, also stand disposed of.
(Ajay Mohan Goel) of Judge 26th October, 2016.
